page: Amazon Web Services m6in.2xlarge is a network-optimized general purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor featuring the x86_64 architecture with 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs via hyperthreading. Memory configuration consists of 32.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include support for AVX-512 vector instructions with VNNI, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic extensions like AES and SHA-NI. The instance provides a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operates without bundled local storage, and includes no dedicated graphics processing units.

Benchmark measurements demonstrate consistent middle-tier performance across varied computational tasks. The instance records 1892.58 in stress-ng single-core execution and 7729.1 in multi-core testing, matching its mid-tier Geekbench scores of 1625.0 single-core and 6029.0 multi-core. Memory throughput reaches 56.93 GB/sec for uncached block reads and 41.85 GB/sec for writes. In-memory data workloads deliver 7.93 million operations per second in Redis SET testing, complemented by 12.0 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Tradeoffs emerge under sustained parallel compression and unaccelerated machine learning; multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and 7B model LLM inference score in the lower percentiles due to the lack of hardware accelerators and restricted core density.

From a resource efficiency perspective, m6in.2xlarge offers balanced hardware density for network-reliant workloads that require dedicated compute threads without the premium overhead of specialized high-memory or GPU systems. The absence of integrated ephemeral storage requires network-attached storage architectures. It is suitable for mid-sized relational databases, caching layers, containerized microservices, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and high-throughput web application backends.
